[Series](index.qmd) · [Foundations](foundations.qmd) · Strings: [Violin](violin.qmd) · Air columns: [Clarinet](clarinet.qmd) · Clamped bars: [Kalimba](kalimba.qmd), [Harmonica](harmonica.qmd) · Stiff strings: **Piano** · Membranes: [Drum](drum.qmd)

A piano string is a violin string that is also a little bit of a kalimba tine. The two restoring forces add, and the overtones creep sharp.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Family: stiff strings
Every real string is slightly stiff, so guitar and harp strings belong here too, faintly. The piano is where stiffness is large enough to hear, and large enough to shape how pianos are tuned.
:::

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple" icon="false"}
## Reader question: why did the piano sound as if the sustain pedal were always down?
Because releasing a key did nothing. The first version let every string ring until it died on its own, and that is exactly what the sustain pedal does. On a real piano each key lifts a felt damper off its strings; letting go drops the damper back and stops the note within a fraction of a second. The sustain pedal lifts all the dampers at once, so released notes keep ringing. The keyboard above now models both. The top 20 keys have no dampers at all, as on a real piano: those short strings die out quickly by themselves.
:::

## Dampers and pedals

A piano has two or three pedals, and none of them touches the operator. They change only how the hammer excites the string, which sets the weights of the modes, and how fast the string loses energy. The frequencies stay where the operator put them.

| Pedal | Usual name | What it does | In the model |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| right | sustain or damper pedal | lifts every damper, so notes ring after the key is released | released notes are not damped |
| left | soft pedal (*una corda* on a grand) | on an upright, moves the hammers closer to the strings so they strike more gently; on a grand, shifts the action so each hammer strikes fewer strings with a softer part of its felt | quieter, and the high partials are weaker |
| middle, on many uprights | practice or mute pedal | lowers a strip of felt between the hammers and the strings | much quieter and muffled: most high partials vanish |

On a grand piano the middle pedal is usually the *sostenuto*, which keeps up only the dampers of keys already held down.

## Deriving the operator

A piano wire is under heavy tension, like a violin string, and it is thick steel, so it also resists bending, like a kalimba tine. Forces per unit length simply add: the tension term from the [foundations](foundations.qmd) and the bending term from the [kalimba](kalimba.qmd) give
$$
\mu\,u_{tt} = T\,u_{xx} - EI\,u_{xxxx}, \qquad\text{that is}\qquad \mathcal{L} = -c^2\partial_x^2 + \kappa^2\partial_x^4 .
$$

Treat the ends as pinned: they cannot move and transmit no bending moment, so $u = u_{xx} = 0$. Real piano strings are held closer to clamped, which shifts the numbers slightly but not the picture.

## Spectrum

Pinned ends make $\sin(n\pi x/L)$ an eigenfunction of both terms at once. Substituting it gives $\omega^2 = c^2k^2 + \kappa^2 k^4$ with $k = n\pi/L$, so
$$
f_n = n f_0\sqrt{1 + Bn^2}, \qquad B = \frac{\pi^2 EI}{T L^2}.
$$

The stiffness constant $B$ is small, but it multiplies $n^2$, so high partials run noticeably sharp. Since $I$ grows like the fourth power of the wire's diameter and $B$ falls like $1/L^2$, short thick treble strings are the stiffest.

```{=html}
<div class="ins">
<div class="panel">

    <svg class="spec" id="pSpec" viewBox="0 0 320 120" aria-label="Partials of the last key played"></svg>
    <div class="readout" id="pPart"></div>
    <p class="cap">Hammer at 1/8 of the length, so the 8th and 16th partials nearly vanish. Try the soft and mute pedals: the stems shrink at the top, but none of them moves.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Why tuners stretch octaves

A tuner sets an octave by listening for beats between the lower note's second partial and the upper note's fundamental. Stiffness pushes that second partial above $2f_0$, so a beat-free octave is slightly wider than 2 : 1. Repeated across the keyboard, this is *stretch tuning*: the top of a piano is tuned sharp of equal temperament, and the bottom flat.

```{=html}
<div class="ins">
<div class="panel">
    <div class="controls"><button id="o21">C4 + C5, exactly 2 : 1</button><button id="ost" class="primary">C4 + C5, stretched</button></div>
    <div class="readout" id="oRead"></div>
    <p class="cap">Listen for the slow wobble in the 2 : 1 version. Raise the stiffness above to speed it up.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<script src="core.js"></script>
<script>
(function () {
  "use strict";
  var C = Core, mult = 1, cache = {}, last = 60, base = 60;
  var LOW = 21, HIGH = 108, WK = 24, UNDAMPED = 89;
  var BLACK = { 1: 1, 3: 1, 6: 1, 8: 1, 10: 1 };
  var CODES = ["KeyA", "KeyW", "KeyS", "KeyE", "KeyD", "KeyF", "KeyT", "KeyG", "KeyY", "KeyH", "KeyU", "KeyJ", "KeyK", "KeyO", "KeyL", "KeyP", "Semicolon", "Quote"];
  var LABEL = ["A", "W", "S", "E", "D", "F", "T", "G", "Y", "H", "U", "J", "K", "O", "L", "P", ";", "'"];
  var ped = { sus: false, soft: false, mute: false }, held = {}, voices = {};
  var kbd = document.getElementById("kbd"), wrap = document.getElementById("kbdwrap"), btn = {}, wi = 0;
  for (var k = LOW; k <= HIGH; k++) if (!BLACK[k % 12]) wi++;
  kbd.style.width = (wi * WK) + "px";
  var x = 0;
  for (var k = LOW; k <= HIGH; k++) {
    var b = document.createElement("button"); b.type = "button"; b.dataset.key = k; b.tabIndex = -1;
    b.setAttribute("aria-label", C.noteName(C.mtof(k)).name);
    if (BLACK[k % 12]) { b.className = "b"; b.style.left = (x * WK - WK * 0.31) + "px"; b.style.width = (WK * 0.62) + "px"; }
    else { b.className = "w"; b.style.left = (x * WK) + "px"; b.style.width = WK + "px"; x++; }
    kbd.appendChild(b); btn[k] = b;
  }
  function labels() {
    for (var k = LOW; k <= HIGH; k++) {
      var i = k - base, inWin = i >= 0 && i < CODES.length, b = btn[k];
      b.classList.toggle("win", inWin);
      b.textContent = inWin ? LABEL[i] : (k % 12 === 0 ? C.noteName(C.mtof(k)).name : "");
    }
    document.getElementById("winRead").innerHTML = "computer keys: <b>" + C.noteName(C.mtof(base)).name + "–" + C.noteName(C.mtof(base + CODES.length - 1)).name + "</b>";
    var el = btn[base]; if (el) wrap.scrollLeft = Math.max(0, parseFloat(el.style.left) - wrap.clientWidth / 2 + 4 * WK);
  }
  function shift(d) { base = Math.max(LOW + (12 - LOW % 12) % 12, Math.min(96, base + 12 * d)); labels(); }
  document.getElementById("octDown").addEventListener("click", function () { shift(-1); });
  document.getElementById("octUp").addEventListener("click", function () { shift(1); });

  function opts() { return { rolloff: ped.mute ? 4.5 : (ped.soft ? 9 : 14) }; }
  function partsFor(k, f1, m) { var o = opts(); o.B = C.models.piano.B(k, m == null ? mult : m); o.f1 = f1 || C.mtof(k); return C.models.piano.partials(o); }
  function buf(k) {
    var id = k + ":" + mult + ":" + ped.soft + ":" + ped.mute;
    if (!cache[id]) {
      var f = C.mtof(k), dur = Math.min(8, 1.5 + 3 * Math.pow(262 / f, 0.6)), b = C.render(C.toHz(partsFor(k), f), dur);
      var d = b.getChannelData(0), n = Math.floor(0.3 * b.sampleRate); for (var i = 0; i < n; i++) d[d.length - 1 - i] *= i / n;
      cache[id] = b;
    }
    return cache[id];
  }
  function level() { return 0.7 * (ped.soft ? 0.55 : 1) * (ped.mute ? 0.25 : 1); }
  function damp(k, tc) {
    var v = voices[k]; if (!v) return; var t = C.ac().currentTime;
    v.g.gain.cancelScheduledValues(t); v.g.gain.setTargetAtTime(0, t, tc || 0.06); v.src.stop(t + 1); delete voices[k];
  }
  function strike(k) {
    if (k < LOW || k > HIGH) return;
    var a = C.ac(); damp(k, 0.01);
    var src = a.createBufferSource(), g = a.createGain(); src.buffer = buf(k); g.gain.value = level();
    src.connect(g); g.connect(C.out); src.start(); voices[k] = { src: src, g: g };
    src.onended = function () { if (voices[k] && voices[k].src === src) delete voices[k]; };
    held[k] = true; btn[k].classList.add("on"); last = k; pspec();
    var nn = C.noteName(C.mtof(k));
    document.getElementById("pRead").innerHTML = "<b>" + nn.name + "</b> · " + C.mtof(k).toFixed(1) + " Hz · B = <b>" + C.models.piano.B(k, mult).toExponential(1) + "</b>" + (k >= UNDAMPED ? " · no damper" : "");
  }
  function release(k) {
    if (!held[k]) return; delete held[k]; btn[k].classList.remove("on");
    if (!ped.sus && k < UNDAMPED) damp(k);
  }
  function setPed(name, on) {
    ped[name] = on; document.getElementById({ sus: "pSus", soft: "pSoft", mute: "pMute" }[name]).setAttribute("aria-pressed", on);
    if (name === "sus" && !on) Object.keys(voices).forEach(function (k) { k = +k; if (!held[k] && k < UNDAMPED) damp(k); });
    if (name !== "sus") pspec();
  }
  document.getElementById("pSus").addEventListener("click", function () { setPed("sus", !ped.sus); });
  document.getElementById("pSoft").addEventListener("click", function () { setPed("soft", !ped.soft); });
  document.getElementById("pMute").addEventListener("click", function () { setPed("mute", !ped.mute); });

  var down = false, curK = -1;
  function keyAt(e) { var el = document.elementFromPoint(e.clientX, e.clientY); return el && el.dataset && el.dataset.key ? +el.dataset.key : -1; }
  kbd.addEventListener("pointerdown", function (e) { e.preventDefault(); down = true; kbd.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId); curK = keyAt(e); if (curK > 0) strike(curK); });
  kbd.addEventListener("pointermove", function (e) { if (!down) return; var k = keyAt(e); if (k !== curK) { if (curK > 0) release(curK); if (k > 0) strike(k); curK = k; } });
  function up() { down = false; if (curK > 0) release(curK); curK = -1; }
  kbd.addEventListener("pointerup", up); kbd.addEventListener("pointercancel", up);
  var codeKey = {};
  window.addEventListener("keydown", function (e) {
    if (e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey || e.altKey || (e.target && e.target.tagName === "INPUT")) return;
    if (e.code === "Space") { e.preventDefault(); if (!e.repeat) setPed("sus", true); return; }
    if (e.code === "KeyZ") { if (!e.repeat) shift(-1); return; }
    if (e.code === "KeyX") { if (!e.repeat) shift(1); return; }
    var i = CODES.indexOf(e.code); if (i < 0 || e.repeat) return;
    e.preventDefault(); var k = base + i; codeKey[e.code] = k; strike(k);
  });
  window.addEventListener("keyup", function (e) {
    if (e.code === "Space") { setPed("sus", false); return; }
    var k = codeKey[e.code]; if (k != null) { delete codeKey[e.code]; release(k); }
  });

  var ms = document.getElementById("mult"), mo = document.getElementById("multo");
  ms.addEventListener("input", function () { mult = parseFloat(ms.value); mo.textContent = mult.toFixed(1); pspec(); octRead(); });
  function pspec() {
    var p = partsFor(last);
    C.stems(document.getElementById("pSpec"), p, { W: 320, H: 120, rmax: 16, fs: 8, sw: 2, labelEvery: 2 });
    var r10 = p[9] ? p[9].ratio : null;
    document.getElementById("pPart").innerHTML = C.noteName(C.mtof(last)).name + " · partial 2 at <b>" + (1200 * Math.log2(p[1].ratio / 2)).toFixed(1) + "¢</b> sharp" + (r10 ? " · partial 10 at <b>" + (1200 * Math.log2(r10 / 10)).toFixed(0) + "¢</b> sharp" : "");
  }
  function r2(k) { var B = C.models.piano.B(k, mult); return 2 * Math.sqrt((1 + 4 * B) / (1 + B)); }
  function octRead() {
    var f = C.mtof(60), beat = f * (r2(60) - 2);
    document.getElementById("oRead").innerHTML = "2 : 1 octave beats at <b>" + beat.toFixed(2) + " Hz</b> · stretched octave is <b>" + (1200 * Math.log2(r2(60) / 2)).toFixed(1) + "¢</b> wide";
  }
  function octave(stretch) {
    var f = C.mtof(60), f5 = stretch ? f * r2(60) : 2 * f;
    var a = C.toHz(partsFor(60, f), f), b = C.toHz(partsFor(72, f5), f5);
    b.forEach(function (p) { p.amp *= 0.8; });
    C.play(C.render(a.concat(b), 4.5), 0.8);
  }
  document.getElementById("o21").addEventListener("click", function () { octave(false); });
  document.getElementById("ost").addEventListener("click", function () { octave(true); });
  C.onTheme(pspec);
  labels(); pspec(); octRead();
  window.addEventListener("load", labels);
})();
</script>
```
